paragraphs.heading: The largest war
paragraphs.text: World War II, or the Second World War, lasted from 1 September 1939 to 2 September 1945. Two coalitions fought it, the Allies and the Axis powers, and almost every country on Earth took part. Many of them waged total war on a scale never seen before. Between 60 and 75 million people died, most of them civilians, making it the deadliest conflict in history.

paragraphs.heading: Roots in the first war
paragraphs.text: World War I had redrawn the map of Europe, and the League of Nations was set up in 1920 to stop another world war. Despite strong pacifist feeling after that war, irredentist and revanchist nationalism grew in several European states, most of all in Germany. The Treaty of Versailles had stripped Germany of roughly 13 per cent of its home territory and every overseas possession, along with reparations and limits on its armed forces. Those unresolved tensions, together with fascism rising in Europe and militarism rising in Japan, were among the war's causes.

paragraphs.heading: Germany strikes first
paragraphs.text: Fighting started on 1 September 1939 with the invasion of Poland by Hitler's Nazi Germany, after which Britain and France declared war on Germany. The Soviet Union also invaded Poland in mid-September, and the two states divided it between them. In 1940 Germany conquered Norway, Denmark, Belgium, Luxembourg and the Netherlands, and France fell that June. Britain and its empire fought on, including in the air over Britain and at sea in the Atlantic.

paragraphs.heading: A world war
paragraphs.text: The Eastern Front opened in June 1941, when Germany attacked the Soviet Union. That December Japan struck American and British territory across Asia and the Pacific, Pearl Harbor in Hawaii among the targets, and the United States entered the war. Japan's push across the Pacific was stopped at the Battle of Midway in June 1942. In early 1943 the Axis lost in North Africa and at Stalingrad, and from then on it was falling back on every front.

paragraphs.heading: The end in 1945
paragraphs.text: In 1944 the Western Allies landed in Normandy in France while the Soviet Union pushed into Central Europe. Berlin fell, and Germany surrendered unconditionally on 8 May 1945. In August the United States dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, and the Soviet Union invaded Japanese-held Manchuria. Japan announced its surrender on 15 August and signed it on 2 September 1945.

paragraphs.heading: The world it left behind
paragraphs.text: The war reshaped politics, economies and societies, and it laid the base for relations between countries for the remainder of the 20th century and beyond. The United Nations was founded to encourage cooperation and prevent future wars, with China, France, the Soviet Union, Britain and the United States as permanent members of its Security Council. The Soviet Union and the United States became rival superpowers, which set up the Cold War. As Europe's great powers lost influence, decolonisation followed in Africa and Asia.
